subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (2, 3, −1) and (7, 8, 5), and B is the matrix with rows (1, 0, 1) and (2, −4, −1), then find A + B.

recall_prompt: Say how you would add these two matrices.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Add entry by entry
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both matrices are 2×3, so addition is defined. Add matching positions — nothing else happens.

recall.must_convey: That the two matrices are the same size and are added entry by entry in matching positions.
accept: both are two by three so add the matching entries
add corresponding entries position by position
matrix addition is entry by entry when the sizes match
rendu same size kabatti corresponding entries add cheyyali
add each entry to the entry in the same place

steps.why: Two matrices can only be added when they have the same number of rows AND columns. Checking the sizes is part of the answer, not a formality.
common_mistakes: Trying to add matrices of different sizes.
Multiplying row by column instead of adding.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Watch the negatives: −1 + 1 = 0 and 8 + (−4) = 4.

recall.must_convey: That the sum has rows (3, 3, 0) and (9, 4, 4).
accept: the answer is three three zero and nine four four
A plus B has rows three three zero and nine four four
the sum matrix is three three zero over nine four four
answer three three zero and nine four four
adding gives a two by three matrix with those entries

steps.why: Adding a negative is subtracting. Both places where that happens here are in the second row.
